question.text: Per the SEBI (Mutual Funds) (Third Amendment) Regulations 2024 cited in NISM Ch 2.4.2.4, the newly-introduced Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) has a minimum investment ticket size of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 2.4.2.4, 'SIFs are sophisticated mutual funds where the minimum required investment amount is Rs. 10 lakhs from the investors across all investment strategies'. The amendment took effect from December 16, 2024. The Trap: Option A (INR 1 crore) is the AIF minimum for non-angel investors. Option B (INR 25 lakh) is a distractor tied to no specific regime. Option D is the ordinary mutual fund minimum for some schemes. Candidates who confuse SIF with AIF pick A. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B distributor exams have started testing SIF post-2024 amendment; XIX-C tests it from the manager's 'do I launch a SIF vs AIF' decision frame. Manager's Pro-Tip: SIF is a strategic alternative to launching an AIF — the MF wrapper gives daily NAV, trustee structure, and lower compliance cost; the INR 10 lakh minimum captures affluent retail that a Cat III AIF (INR 1 cr min) misses. Evaluate SIF before you file the PPM for a new Cat III.
